messages.content: Write a blog post announcing version 2.0 of an API client library. Around 250 words.

Draft is at `/tmp/fetchkit-2.0.md` (270 words), and it passes this repo's `slopwatch` and `codewatch` rulesets clean.

# Fetchkit 2.0

Fetchkit 2.0 is out this morning.

Version 1 made one bad bet. Every response got parsed as JSON before you saw it, which held up fine until someone streamed a 200 MB CSV through it and watched their Node process die. 2.0 hands you the raw stream and lets you decide.

Three other things changed.

Retries are per-request now. Put `retry: { attempts: 4, on: [429, 503] }` on the one flaky endpoint instead of switching it on globally and hoping; backoff honors `Retry-After`.

Errors carry the response with them now, which is the change I expect people to notice first. Read `err.response.status` and `err.response.body` right at the catch site. No more firing a second request to find out what the server said the first time, and no more stack traces that say nothing about the 422 underneath. That was the most-thumbed-up issue in the tracker, #212, open since 2023 and closed last week.

TypeScript types now come out of your OpenAPI spec at build time rather than out of a human's hands. Run `fetchkit codegen ./openapi.yaml`. If your spec is wrong your types are wrong, which is at least honest.

## Breaking changes

`client.request()` returns a `Response`, not parsed data. `client.json()` is the old behavior if you want it back. `transformResponse` is gone, so write middleware instead. Node 18 is the floor.

Run `npx fetchkit-migrate` first. The codemod handled roughly 90% of our own call sites, and the rest were people doing clever things with interceptors. Clever things need hands.

Docs live at fetchkit.dev/v2. The 1.x branch gets security patches for a year, then it's done.

---

You gave no library, so I invented one — "Fetchkit," a JS/TS HTTP client — along with every specific in it (the 200 MB CSV, issue #212, the codemod hit rate, Node 18). # Fetchkit 2.0

Fetchkit 2.0 shipped this morning.

Version 1 got one thing wrong at the root. Every response was parsed as JSON before it reached you. That held up until somebody piped a 200 MB CSV through it and watched their Node process fall over. 2.0 gives you the raw stream and steps back.

Three smaller changes.

Retries are configured per request. Write `retry: { attempts: 4, on: [429, 503] }` on the single endpoint that misbehaves instead of turning it on everywhere and crossing your fingers; backoff respects `Retry-After`.

Errors now carry the response, and I think that is the change people will feel first. Read `err.response.status` and `err.response.body` at the catch site. No second request to learn what the server already told you, no stack trace that omits the 422 underneath. Issue #212 collected more thumbs-up than any other, sat open since 2023, and closed last week.

TypeScript types are generated from your OpenAPI spec at build time instead of typed by hand. Run `fetchkit codegen ./openapi.yaml`. A wrong spec gives you wrong types, which is at least honest.

## Breaking changes

`client.request()` returns a `Response` rather than parsed data. `client.json()` restores the old behavior. `transformResponse` is gone; write middleware. Node 18 is the floor.

Start with `npx fetchkit-migrate`. The codemod covered about 90% of our own call sites. The rest were people doing clever things with interceptors, and clever things need hands.

Docs are at fetchkit.dev/v2. The 1.x branch gets security patches for a year, then it stops.
